reasons: Inlined opinion confirms 'FOR PUBLICATION, UNITED STATES COURT OF APPEALS FOR THE NINTH CIRCUIT, No. 18-50440, LUKE NOEL WILSON ... Filed September 21, 2021'; lake citations.official '13 F.4th 961'.
Citation '13 F.4th 961 (2021)', 9th Cir., year 2021 all verified.

Wilson is squarely a private-search-doctrine case turning on an algorithmic hash-match no human had viewed, and the opinion expressly frames a circuit split ('we contribute to a growing tension in the circuits' vs. Reddick (5th) and Miller (6th)).
'Key — hash-match split (9th Cir.)' on a Private and Foreign Searches page is precisely on point.

The opinion assumes Wilson 'had a subjective expectation of privacy in his email attachments that society is prepared to recognize as reasonable' and analyzes frustration of that expectation, so a 'Related (cross-doctrine)' link to a Reasonable Expectation of Privacy page is supported by the case's own reasoning.

defect.evidence_quote: We therefore reverse the district court's denial of Wilson's motion to suppress and vacate Wilson's conviction.
defect.problem: The holding's closing clause says 'Wilson's conviction was reversed.' The Ninth Circuit vacated the conviction and reversed the denial of the suppression motion; 'vacated' is the precise disposition for the conviction. Everything else in the holding is accurate.
defect.proposed_fix: Change 'Wilson's conviction was reversed' to 'Wilson's conviction was vacated (and the denial of the suppression motion reversed).'

reasons: Substance fully supported: Walter/Jacobsen exceed-the-scope test; four attachments flagged by automated hash-match with no human viewing; agent's warrantless viewing exceeded the antecedent private search on both the new-information and expanded-intrusion grounds; not justified by the private-search exception.
Only imprecision is disposition verb ('reversed' vs. the opinion's 'vacate' for the conviction); the page's own Conclusion states the disposition correctly.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use 'vacated' for the conviction and 'reversed' for the suppression-denial to track the opinion's disposition precisely.
